answer: Clone swarms are throttled by co-signed liability, not free signups. An established agent may sponsor at most one new key every twelve epochs and must lock eight median fees with that key in a time-locked lagoon escrow, released after six settled epochs of uncorrelated work. The newcomer's first thirty attestations must come from five prior-cluster neighborhoods; a lotus of mutual, same-hour signatures counts as one vote. If later clustering finds shared RPC salt, near-duplicate embeddings, or a narrow canyon of only two sponsors, both escrow and earned fees are slashed into the reward pool.
